title: German zirconia, finished by hand
body: Every veneer, crown and bridge we make is zirconia milled from German-made discs and finished by our ceramist in the same building as your doctor. Three things that changes:

features.alt: A multilayer zirconia disc on its edge showing five bands from warm ivory to translucent white, next to a single-shade lithium disilicate ingot and a thin translucent wafer
features.title: Built into the material, not painted on
features.text: Our discs come with five layers of shade: warmer at the gum, more translucent toward the edge. On front teeth the ceramist adds surface texture and enamel effects by hand, on top of a gradient that is already there.

features.alt: Close-up of a front tooth restored with a zirconia crown whose edge meets healthy pink gum with no dark line
features.title: Finished at the gum line, not under it
features.text: Zirconia does not discolor, so the edge can sit where it is visible, cleaned and sealed. The fibers that attach your gum to the tooth stay intact, which is what keeps gum and bone where they are.

features.alt: A ceramist's gloved hands refining the edge of a zirconia crown with a fine polishing bur under a bench magnifier
features.title: Seated and sealed by hand
features.text: Milled crowns rarely fit straight off the machine. Each one is adjusted under magnification with fine burs until it seats without pressure, then the margin is polished into a closed seal that keeps bacteria out.

glance.label: Strength
glance.sub: About twice the strength of conventional porcelain. Takes back teeth and grinders.

glance.label: Tooth removed
glance.sub: 0.3 mm of preparation for veneers, 0.5 mm walls for crowns. Most of your natural tooth stays.

glance.label: Designed for
glance.sub: Zirconia does not stain, change shade or chip at the edge with normal care.

head: Zirconia at Xiluet Smiles
Lithium disilicate (e.max)
rows: Strength
About 1,000 to 1,200 MPa. Takes the bite of back teeth and grinders.
About 470 MPa, the manufacturer's figure. Chips more often under heavy load and in bridges.
Crowns: tooth removed
0.5 mm walls, so less of your tooth is cut away.
1.0 mm walls with adhesive cementation. More reduction.
Veneers: tooth removed
0.3 mm, and on some teeth none.
0.3 mm is possible; most labs ask for 0.5 to 0.7 mm.
Where the edge sits
At the gum line, where it can be seen, cleaned and kept sealed. The gum attachment and bone underneath are left alone.
Often placed under the gum to hide the cement line. Edges under the gum are linked to inflammation, recession and bone loss over time.
Shade and translucency
Five layers built into the disc: warmer at the gum, more translucent toward the edge. The gradient is in the material itself.
A single-shade block. Translucency at the edge has to be cut back and added by hand as an extra layer, one more step and one more interface that can chip.
Color over time
Does not stain or change shade.
The porcelain is stable; the bonded edge can pick up stain over the years.
Expected lifespan
Designed for 20 years. 5-year written warranty.
10 to 15 years is typical; chipping is the usual reason for replacement.

footnote: Strength figures are the manufacturers' biaxial flexural values for 3Y zirconia and IPS e.max; thickness minimums are the manufacturers' published guidance. How long any restoration lasts depends on bite, gum health and care. Our warranty terms are written into every plan.
